content:
No, Einstein did not win the Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity. He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921** (officially received in 1922) for his explanation of the **photoelectric effect**, which was a crucial contribution to the development of quantum theory.

The Nobel Committee at the time was cautious about awarding the prize for relativity because it was still considered controversial and not yet fully verified by experimental evidence. The photoelectric effect, on the other hand, had clear experimental support and was a foundational discovery in quantum mechanics.

Einstein's work on relativity (both Special and General Relativity) is undoubtedly one of the greatest scientific achievements of the 20th century, but it was not the reason for his Nobel Prize.
